# Context-Rich Solid Mechanics Problem

## End Milling — Combined Bending and Torsion of an End Mill

### Engineering Context

A manufacturing engineer is reviewing a light end-milling operation on an Aluminum 6061 workpiece. As the rotating cutter engages the workpiece, transverse cutting force bends the exposed tool and a tangential force component produces torque about its axis. The exposed cutter is idealized as a solid circular cantilever fixed at the holder face.

The machining context follows Suraidah et al. (2020), including an HSS end mill on Aluminum 6061 and measured radial, tangential, and axial cutting-force components. The assigned forces are representative light-cutting design loads rather than exact experimental readings. The effective overhang is an instructor-selected modeling value, and heat-treated M2 high-speed steel is used as a separate representative material-property basis for the static strength idealization. The complete six calculation inputs appear after the modeling questions.

### Main Engineering Goal

Determine the nominal bending and torsional stresses at the critical outer surface of the exposed cutter, combine them with the von Mises criterion, and assess the simplified static factor of safety. Then determine the transverse force associated with the required factor of safety when the baseline tangential-to-transverse force ratio remains 2/3.

### System Components

- vertical milling-machine spindle;
- tool holder or collet, idealized as the fixed restraint;
- exposed end mill, idealized as the critical solid circular cantilever;
- Aluminum 6061 workpiece and its fixture; and
- machine table and structure carrying the reactions.
